proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (penalty 0.337) and LiF (penalty 0.310) were both insulating with wide gaps, but both reacted with Li6PS5Cl at equilibrium, and both sit far above the 0.05 eV target. A different anion family is needed, and a silicate is the most chemically distinct option not yet tested.

proposal.hypothesis: Li6Zr2O7 is a Li-rich zirconate with Zr4+ centers, which are very hard to reduce, so it should be stable against the sulfide electrolyte and oxidatively stable at 4 V against LiCoO2. The earlier coatings with Li3PO4, LiF and LiAlSiO4 all showed penalties of 0.20 eV/non-Li atom or more from reaction products (P/S-O, S/Cl, Al/Cl/S). A Zr4+ oxide framework with a high Li content may limit these reactions and bring the penalty down. Its band gap should be wide, so it should remain insulating.
proposal.motivation: LiAlSiO4 gave the lowest penalty so far (0.204) among fully oxidized, wide-gap insulators, suggesting that oxide frameworks with high-valent, hard-to-reduce cations perform better than phosphate or fluoride chemistries. Li6Zr2O7 extends this trend to Zr4+ and a higher Li content.

proposal.hypothesis: LiSiBO4 is a fully oxidized borosilicate with Si4+ and B3+ centers that are hard to reduce by the sulfide electrolyte. It is a borate family member, which has not been tested yet. Its lack of Al3+ may avoid the Al-containing products (AlCl3, Al2S3-type) seen with LiAlSiO4, and its oxide framework should keep it oxidatively stable at 4 V against LiCoO2 while remaining wide-gap and insulating.
proposal.motivation: LiAlSiO4 gave the lowest penalty so far (0.204 eV/non-Li atom), which points toward oxide frameworks with high-valent, hard-to-reduce cations. Li3PO4 and LiF gave much larger penalties (0.337 and 0.310), and Li6Zr2O7 was worse (0.743, with self-decomposition). LiSiBO4 keeps the oxide and silicate character while changing the cation set away from Al and Zr.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3Al(BO3)2 is a fully oxidized, wide-gap borate with Al3+ and B3+ centers that are hard to reduce by the sulfide electrolyte. It keeps the Al3+ cation that gave the lowest penalty so far (LiAlSiO4, 0.204) while moving to a borate framework that has not been tested with Al. Its Li-rich composition may limit Li-depleting reactions with Li6PS5Cl, and it should remain oxidatively stable at 4 V against LiCoO2.
proposal.motivation: LiAlSiO4 (mp-aaaaajjj) gave the lowest equilibrated penalty so far (0.204 eV/non-Li atom) among insulating, wide-gap oxides, and LiSiBO4 showed that borate chemistry can reduce the penalty further (0.177). Combining Al3+ with a borate framework tests whether that trend holds.

proposal.hypothesis: Li5Al(SiO4)2 is a Li-rich aluminosilicate with fully oxidized Al3+ and Si4+ centers that are hard to reduce by the sulfide electrolyte. Compared with LiAlSiO4, its higher Li content may suppress Li-depleting interfacial reactions with Li6PS5Cl, and its oxide framework should stay oxidatively stable near 4 V against LiCoO2 and remain wide-gap.
proposal.motivation: LiAlSiO4 (mp-aaaaajjj) gave the lowest penalty among the insulating oxides so far (0.204 eV/non-Li atom). LiSiBO4 (0.177) and Li3Al(BO3)2 (0.378) showed that the Al-containing products and composition matter, so a more Li-rich aluminosilicate is the closest informed step.

proposal.hypothesis: Li4Ca(BO3)2 is a Li-rich orthoborate with Ca2+ and B3+ centers, which are hard to reduce by the sulfide electrolyte. Its high Li content may limit Li-depleting reactions with Li6PS5Cl. Unlike the Al-containing candidates, which formed AlCl3/AlPO4/Al-sulfate products, it avoids Al and should stay oxidatively stable near 4 V against LiCoO2 while remaining wide-gap.
proposal.motivation: The lowest penalties so far came from borate and aluminosilicate oxides (LiSiBO4 at 0.177, LiAlSiO4 at 0.204). Al-containing products drove the higher penalties (Li3Al(BO3)2 at 0.378, Li5Al(SiO4)2 at 0.533). An Al-free, Li-rich borate tests whether the borate advantage holds without Al.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3BO3 is a Li-rich orthoborate with fully oxidized B3+ centers that are hard to reduce by the sulfide electrolyte. Borate chemistry gave the lowest penalty so far (LiSiBO4, 0.177 eV/non-Li atom), and this compound keeps that B-O framework while adding Li content and avoiding Al, Zr and Ca, which formed the costly Al/Zr/Ca chloride, sulfate and phosphate products. It should be wide-gap and oxidatively stable near 4 V against LiCoO2.
proposal.motivation: LiSiBO4 (mp-aaaaandi) gave the lowest equilibrated penalty so far (0.177), showing borate frameworks can beat the Al-containing and phosphate contacts. Li4Ca(BO3)2 was worse (0.585), mainly from Ca-containing products, so the next test is a Li-rich borate with no alkaline-earth or Al cation.

proposal.hypothesis: LiBO2 is a simple, fully oxidized Li-B-O borate with B3+ centers that are hard to reduce by Li6PS5Cl. Borate chemistry gave the lowest penalty so far (LiSiBO4, 0.177 eV/non-Li atom), and LiBO2 keeps that B-O framework without Si, Al, Zr, Ca or Zn cations that formed the costly chloride, sulfate and phosphate products. Its wide gap and oxide character should keep it insulating and oxidatively stable near 4 V against LiCoO2.
proposal.motivation: LiSiBO4 (mp-aaaaandi) gave the lowest equilibrated penalty so far (0.177). Li3BO3 (0.725) and Li3Al(BO3)2 (0.378) showed that the borate advantage depends on the cation set and Li content, so a simpler Li:B = 1:1 borate is the next informed test.
